svg.text: HAEBOT / KIRO | PHOTO WIRING GUIDE
2. E-stop + contactor - what connects where
One NC mechanically latching mushroom; no START button, auxiliary holding loop or reset controller.
Your photographed unit: label 500A DC12V
Identify the LARGE main studs and SMALL coil studs on the actual device.
Do not assign + / - to a small stud from its left/right position in this picture.
MAIN POWER - large studs
From protected BATT_MON
After F1 + SW1 + Matek shunt
K1 MAIN CONTACT → U3 → FB1
Feed wheels, arm 1 and arm 2 from this path
COIL CONTROL - small studs
F5 2 A*
E-STOP
NC - LATCHING
K1 COIL
Positive: feed through the E-stop NC pair
Negative: return to battery-negative bus
Polarity / suppression / continuous duty: verify
Fused control feed
Battery negative / POWER_GND
USE THE NC CONTACT PAIR
Released/unpressed: NC contacts are CLOSED → coil receives power.
Push: NC contacts OPEN → coil drops out → motor power is cut.
Let go: mushroom stays locked down → motor power stays OFF.
Twist to release: NC closes → coil energises → motor power returns.
NC terminal numbers vary (for example 11-12 or 1-2). Read the block.
Check continuity with all power disconnected before fitting the switch.
BEFORE CONNECTING THE BATTERY
K1 must support continuous coil energisation at the actual pack voltage.
Verify the coil current before accepting the 2 A control fuse / switch rating.
D1 suppression is still TBD: follow the contactor manufacturer, not a guessed diode.
The red mushroom is an illustration of the required type, not a selected product.
This simple circuit has NO restart interlock; restoring supply also enables power.
Arm holding torque disappears when power is cut; support arms during first tests.
A 500 A label alone does not establish DC breaking capability.
A welded K1 contact can defeat this single-contactor power cut.
Rev B pictorial supplement | 2026-11-26 | * = provisional rating | Drawing positions do not establish terminal polarity.
Follow actual + / - / NC markings. Battery BMS, K1 continuous duty / coil / suppression and I2C pin mapping still need verification.
